edition.name: Migne, Patrologia Latina (PL 2, Paris 1844), De jejuniis, via Latin Wikisource transcription
edition.witness_note: Single locked witness in repo; second witness not yet locked.

source_text: Mirarer Psychicos si sola luxuria tenderentur, qua saepius nubunt; et non etiam ingluvie lacerarentur, qua jejunia oderunt, monstrum scilicet haberetur libido sine gula, cum duo haec tam unita atque concreta sint, ut si disjungi omnino potuissent, ipsi prius ventri pudenda non adhaererent. Specta corpus, et una regio est. Denique pro dispositione membrorum, ordo vitiorum; prior venter, et statim caetera saginae substructa lascivia est. Per edacitatem salacitas transit. Agnosco igitur animalem fidem studio carnis qua tota constat, tam multivorantiae quam multinubentiae pronam; ut merito spiritalem disciplinam pro substantia aemulam, in hac quoque specie continentiae accuset, proinde gulae frenos induentem per nullas interdum vel seras vel aridas escas, quemadmodum et libidini per unicas nuptias. Piget jam cum talibus congredi, pudet et jam de eis altercari, quorum nec defensio verecunda est. Quomodo enim protegam castitatem et sobrietatem sine taxatione adversariorum? Quinam isti sint semel nominabo exteriores et interiores botuli Psychicorum. Hi Paracleto controversiam faciunt; propter hoc novae prophetiae recusantur: non quod alium Deum praedicent Montanus et Priscilla et Maximilla, nec quod Jesum Christum solvant, nec quod aliquam fidei aut spei regulam evertant; sed quod plane doceant saepius jejunare, quam nubere. De modo quidem nubendi jam edidimus monogamiae defensionem. Nunc de castigatione victus, secunda, vel magis prima continentiae pugna est. Arguunt nos, quod jejunia propria custodiamus; quod stationes plerumque in vesperam producamus; quod etiam xerophagias observemus, siccantes cibum ab omni carne, et omni jurulentia, et uvidioribus quibusque pomis, ne quid vinositatis vel edamus vel potemus; lavacri quoque abstinentiam, congruentem arido victui. Novitatem igitur abjectant, de cujus inlicito praescribant, aut haeresim judicandam, si humana praesumptio est, aut pseudoprophetiam pronuntiandam, si spiritalis indictio est, dum quaqua ex parte anathema audiamus, qui aliter adnuntiamus.
pass_a_gloss: I would wonder at the Psychics if they were inclined only to luxury, by which they more often are covered, and not also were torn by gluttony, by which they hate fasts, for surely lust without gluttony would be considered a monstrosity, since these two are so united and intertwined, that if they could be completely separated, they would not even first adhere to the shameful parts of the belly. Look at the body, and it is one region. Finally, according to the arrangement of the members, there is an order of vices; the belly comes first, and immediately the rest are built up by lust. Through gluttony, lust passes. I recognize therefore the animal faith, which consists entirely of the desire of the flesh, prone to both much eating and much marrying; so that spiritual discipline, which is a rival of the substance, rightly accuses it in this kind of self-control, putting a bridle on the gluttony through sometimes even dry or barren foods, just as it does to lust through single marriages. I am already ashamed to engage with such people, I am also ashamed to argue with them, whose defense is not modest. For how can I protect chastity and sobriety without accusing their opponents? What kind of people are they, I will name them once, the external and internal parasites of the Psychics. These make a controversy with the Paraclete; because of this, new prophecies are rejected: not because they preach another God, Montanus and Priscilla and Maximilla, nor because they dissolve Jesus Christ, nor because they overturn any rule of faith or hope; but because they plainly teach to fast more often than to marry. We have already published a defense of monogamy regarding the manner of marrying. Now, regarding the chastisement of food, there is a second, or rather a first, battle of self-control. They accuse us because we keep our own fasts; because we often prolong our stations until evening; because we also observe xerophagies, drying food from all meat, and all juice, and any moist fruits, so that we may not eat or drink anything with a wine-like quality; we also abstain from bathing, which is consistent with a dry diet. Therefore, they reject the novelty, of which they prescribe the illegitimacy, or they judge it a heresy, if it is a human presumption, or they declare it a false prophecy, if it is a spiritual indictment, while we hear anathema from every side, because we announce it differently.

pass_b_english: I would be astonished if the Psychics were driven only by luxury — the vice that makes them marry so often — and not also torn apart by gluttony, the vice that makes them hate fasting. For lust without gluttony would be a monstrosity, since these two are so tightly fused that if they could be completely separated, the genitals would never have stuck to the belly in the first place. Look at the body: it is one continuous region. And just as the members are arranged, so the vices line up: the belly comes first, and immediately the rest are built up by lust. Gluttony is the gateway to lechery. I therefore recognize their animal faith for what it is — a life powered entirely by fleshly appetite, prone to both massive eating and serial marrying. Spiritual discipline, the rival of that substance, rightly indicts it on this front of self-control too, putting a bridle on gluttony by sometimes prescribing even dry or meager rations, just as it curbs lust by limiting marriage to a single union. I am fed up with engaging such people; I am ashamed even to argue with them, since their defense has no shame. How else can I defend chastity and sobriety without calling out their opponents? Let me name them once for all: the external and internal parasites of the Psychics.

They pick a fight with the Paraclete; that is why the new prophecies are rejected — not because Montanus, Priscilla, and Maximilla preach another God, or dissolve Jesus Christ, or overturn any rule of faith or hope, but because they plainly teach people to fast more often than to marry. We have already published a defense of monogamy on the manner of marrying. Now, regarding the discipline of diet, there is a second — or rather the first — battle of self-control. They accuse us because we keep our own fasts; because we often extend our fast-days until evening; because we also observe xerophagies, drying our food of all meat, all juice, and every moist fruit, so that we neither eat nor drink anything with a wine-like quality; and because we abstain from bathing, which suits a dry diet. So they reject the novelty, prescribing its illegitimacy, or they judge it a heresy if it is human presumption, or they denounce it as a false prophecy if it is a spiritual indictment — while we hear anathema from every side, simply because we proclaim it differently.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Latin text. Pass A and Pass B are consistent with the source. The translation of 'pudenda' as 'shameful parts' (A) and 'genitals' (B) is a valid interpretation of the Latin term for lewd/shameful things. The distinction between the Montanists' error (fasting vs marrying) and their orthodoxy (God, Christ, faith/hope) is preserved. All clauses, including the list of xerophagic restrictions, are accounted for.

source_identity: 'Psychicos' is correctly translated as 'Psychics' (Latin 'Psychicos'), and 'Paracleto' is correctly translated as 'Paraclete' (referring to the Holy Spirit). scripture: No scriptural citations are present in the source text, so no issues here.
